messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed spikes in unique span attributes in the telemetry index. Looks like prompt_hash and request_id are flooding the cardinality.

mira: Yep saw that in the retention dashboard. Query counts for span.attr.prompt_hash jumped x6 after the new chat routing rollout.

sasha: That explains slow queries for per-route latency graphs. We didn't scrub prompt hash at ingest for user-facing services.

alex: Proposal: quarantine high-cardinality attrs at the ingest layer and move a hashed/bucketed fingerprint to the exporter. Keep original attr only for a short TTL in a separate ephemeral store for debugging.

taylor: Can you sketch the flow? Are we talking OTLP exporter-level redaction or collector-side?

alex: Collector-side scrub + ephemeral store. Rough sketch:
```
receive span 
if attr in HIGH_CARDINALITY_ALLOWLIST then
  store ephemeral(attr) with TTL 6h in kv-store
  replace attr with bucket(hash(attr, salt), N_BUCKETS)
else
  pass through
end
```
The KV lookup id would be a per-tenant opaque id so only support can map back via audit access.

mira: I like ephemeral store for debugging, but two immediate questions: where do we store salt for hash? and how do we avoid it becoming another sensitive secret?

sasha: If salt is per-cluster and rotated, risk is limited. But it does mean hashes change on rotation and hurts correlation across rotations. Maybe we version the salt and include salt_version in the bucketed attr.

taylor: We also need to think about quota/billing impact. If we still write ephemeral raw attrs to a KV store, that could balloon write ops. Maybe sample the ephemeral capture (1%) for low-pri tenants and 100% for enterprise when requested.

alex: Agreed. Add sampling + tenant policy. Default: capture only when request has trace.sampled_for_debug flag or tenant is on an allowlist. For everyone else, capture only 0.1% by default.

mira: Operational concern: where do we implement the allowlist and rollout UX? Product wants a toggle in Console to mark tenants for full debug capture. We should design the API for that.

sasha: Console feature: per-tenant telemetry settings -> scrub mode (drop/hash/bucket), ephemeral-debug (on/off), sample_rate. That maps to a config in the control-plane which the collector pulls.

alex: Another debate: Do we hash prompt contents or prompt_id? For many integrations we only have full prompt text. Hashing reduces cardinality but still leaks token-level entropy. We should normalize whitespace and trim nonsemantic chars before hashing so similar prompts map together.

taylor: Also need to document expected utility loss. Bucketing collapses distinct prompts — will affect prompt-level regression alerts. We should ensure Redwood Optimize evals can use raw prompts if customer opts in.

mira: Security: ephemeral store must be encrypted at rest and access controlled by a support-only role with just-in-time access logging. Audit trail mandatory.

alex: On exporter discussions: debate between doing scrubbing in the SDKs vs collector. SDK-level gives early PII removal but means many SDKs to update. Collector-side gives uniform behavior and can be rolled out independently. I prefer collector-first with SDK opt-in later.

sasha: Agreed. Collector-first also lets us enforce network-level policies for private deployments. But we need an opt-in flag for hosted customers wanting raw spans for a period.

ingest-bot: deploy plan created: collector scrub v1 -> staging (canary 1%) -> rollout window 48h -> rollback on error.

alex: For telemetry retention and indexing, we should add a new low-card index for bucketed attrs and aggressive TTL (30d), and avoid any long-term indexing of raw prompt hashes. Ephemeral store covers short-term debugging.

taylor: Can we re-run historical regressions that rely on raw prompt hashes? If not, how do we support customers who need historical prompt-level metrics?

mira: That would require explicit opt-in and storage costs. We should let customers export raw telemetry to their own S3 if they want long-term raw retention. Console can show an export workflow.

alex: Next steps I propose: 1) PR for collector scrub draft config 2) design doc for ephemeral KV store + sampling policy 3) Console feature spec for tenant telemetry toggles 4) rollout plan with safety gates and metrics (cardinality, query latency, error rates).

sasha: I'll take the PR for the collector config.

taylor: I'll draft the Console spec and the export workflow.

mira: I'll write the security/audit requirements for ephemeral storage and salt rotation.

deploy-bot: collector-scrub-v1 deployed to staging at 2024-06-15T21:10:12Z (canary=1%).

alex: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to review the PR and the Console mocks. :thumbsup:
